title: Apple Scab
content:
Disease: Apple Scab
Cause: Fungal disease caused by Venturia inaequalis.
Symptoms: Olive-green to dark lesions can develop on leaves and fruit. Severe infections may cause leaf distortion and premature leaf drop.
Management: Remove infected fallen leaves and plant debris. Maintain good orchard sanitation and follow locally recommended disease-management practices.
Prevention: Use resistant cultivars where available and maintain good sanitation and appropriate irrigation practices.

title: Apple Black Rot
content:
Disease: Apple Black Rot
Cause: Fungal disease associated with Botryosphaeria obtusa.
Symptoms: Dark lesions may develop on leaves and fruit, with fruit rot appearing as the disease progresses.
Management: Remove infected plant material and maintain orchard sanitation.
Prevention: Use good sanitation and remove diseased or mummified fruit.

title: Apple Cedar Apple Rust
content:
Disease: Apple Cedar Apple Rust
Cause: Fungal disease caused by Gymnosporangium species.
Symptoms: Yellow or orange spots can develop on leaves, sometimes followed by tissue damage and premature defoliation.
Management: Monitor symptoms and maintain orchard sanitation.
Prevention: Use resistant cultivars where available and manage nearby alternate hosts when appropriate.

title: Apple Healthy
content:
Disease: Apple Healthy
Cause: No disease detected.
Symptoms: Leaves generally show normal healthy green coloration without characteristic disease lesions.
Management: Continue normal plant care and monitoring.
Prevention: Maintain good sanitation, irrigation and general plant health.

Management: Follow local citrus disease-management guidance and manage vectors where appropriate.
Prevention: Use healthy planting material and follow locally recommended vector-management practices.

title: Tomato Leaf Mold
content:
Disease: Tomato Leaf Mold
Cause: Fungal disease caused by Passalora fulva.
Symptoms: Yellowish leaf spots and mold growth may develop, particularly under humid conditions.
Management: Improve ventilation and remove severely affected leaves where appropriate.
Prevention: Reduce humidity and maintain good airflow.

title: Tomato Septoria Leaf Spot
content:
Disease: Tomato Septoria Leaf Spot
Cause: Fungal disease caused by Septoria lycopersici.
Symptoms: Small circular leaf spots with dark margins may develop.
Management: Remove infected leaves and maintain sanitation.
Prevention: Avoid overhead irrigation and remove infected debris.

title: Tomato Two-Spotted Spider Mite
content:
Disease: Tomato Two-Spotted Spider Mite
Cause: Damage caused by two-spotted spider mites.
Symptoms: Fine stippling, discoloration and webbing may occur on leaves.
Management: Monitor mite populations and use locally recommended integrated pest-management practices.
Prevention: Maintain plant health and monitor foliage regularly.

title: Tomato Target Spot
content:
Disease: Tomato Target Spot

Symptoms: Circular brown lesions with concentric rings may develop on leaves and fruit.
Management: Remove infected material and maintain good sanitation.
Prevention: Improve airflow and avoid prolonged leaf wetness.

title: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus
content:
Disease: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus
Cause: Viral disease transmitted primarily by whiteflies.
Symptoms: Leaf curling, yellowing, stunted growth and reduced fruit development may occur.
Management: Manage vectors and follow locally recommended viral-disease practices.
Prevention: Use healthy planting material and appropriate vector management.

title: Tomato Mosaic Virus
content:
Disease: Tomato Mosaic Virus
Cause: Viral disease caused by Tomato mosaic virus.
Symptoms: Mosaic patterns, leaf distortion and reduced plant growth may occur.
Management: Remove infected plants where appropriate and maintain sanitation.
Prevention: Use clean planting material and disinfect tools.
